text:
sara: Heads-up — bringing up 13B-nf4 on dedicated pool and hitting intermittent OOMs when batch_size>1 and long replies. Happens on NVIDIA A100-40GB. Logs show CUDA OOM allocating KV cache around token 512+. Anyone seen fragmentation here?

vikram: Which runtime version? we had a batcher regression in prod last week that increased memory pressure.

sara: runtime v2.8.1-prod. perf-bot: automated snapshot uploaded https://perf.redwood/snapshots/1763401234 (contains nvidia-smi and torch summaries).

vikram: Two quick experiments to try: 1) reduce default max_new_tokens for that route to 128 so clients can't request huge outputs by mistake; 2) try tuning CUDA allocator to reduce fragmentation: set env var `TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128,garbage_collection_threshold:0.6` and restart worker process. Also shrink batcher settings for the model: `max_batch_size: 2`, `max_batch_tokens: 2048`, `max_latency_ms: 30`.

joel: Also consider toggling continuous batching off for this model — continuous batching can grow KV allocations across micro-batches and blows memory for long seqs. Set `continuous_batching: false` in the model route. If you need throughput, we can try token-aware batching instead (group by seq len).

marie: FYI we've seen small quality regressions with nf4 at seq_len > 1024 on the eval deck (more hallucinations). If you reduce max_new_tokens you can avoid the worst-case quality+mem failure combo. Consider a fallback policy: nf4 for short outputs, int8 fallback for long outputs.

vikram: If you repro, please capture these at failure time: `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_gpu_memory --format=csv`, `python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.memory_summary())"`, and the worker log around allocation failure. Paste the logs here.

perf-bot: Memory snapshot and aggregated allocation traces are at https://perf.redwood/snapshots/1763401234/trace.tar.gz

sara: I'm going to change the route defaults now: set `max_new_tokens: 128`, `continuous_batching: false`, `max_batch_size: 2`. Will restart 3 workers and run the long-response regen test. Will report back with logs. :thumbsup:

joel: If OOM persists after those, we should run a dev build with `--compact-kv-cache` (experiment) and try preallocating max KV for worst-case seq len to avoid fragmentation.

sara: Sounds good. I'll post results here in ~30m.
